extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, Patent Office officials, and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory standards and procedural rules from 19th-century United States patent acts governing applications, examinations, appeals, fees, marking, models, patent terms, and office procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of bill and payment of expenses when no opposing party
rubrics_metrics.description: In all cases where there is no opposing party, a copy of the bill shall be served upon the Commissioner of Patents, when the whole of the expenses of the proceeding shall be paid by the applicant, whether the final decision shall be in his favor or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirement: serve Commissioner and applicant bears all expenses regardless of outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Chief Justice of the District Court of Columbia (1839)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an appeal is allowed by law from the decision of the Commissioner to a board of examiners, the party shall have a right, instead, to appeal to the Chief Justice of the District Court of the United States for the District of Columbia by giving notice to the commissioner, filing reasons of appeal specifically set forth in writing within such time as the commissioner shall appoint, and paying into the Patent Office, to the credit of the patent fund, the sum of twenty-five dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief Justice must hear and determine appeals summary on evidence produced before the commissioner, after notifying the commissioner and interested parties. The commissioner must lay before the judge original papers, evidence, and written grounds of his decision; the judge's revision is confined to points involved by the reasons of appeal. At request, commissioner and examiners may be examined under oath to explain principles of the machine or other thing. The judge returns all papers with certificate of proceedings and decision, which shall be entered of record and govern further proceedings of the commissioner. The judge's opinion does not preclude later contesting of patent validity in any other judicial court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner power to make regulations for taking evidence in contested cases (1839/act of 1842 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents shall have power to make all such regulations, in respect to the taking of evidence to be used in contested cases before him, as may be just and reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Commissioner authority to prescribe rules for evidence-taking in Patent Office contested cases; also notes repeal of prior board-of-examiners provisions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation to Chief Justice for appeals (1839)
rubrics_metrics.description: There be paid annually, out of the patent fund, to the said Chief Justice, in consideration of the duties herein imposed, the sum of one hundred dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative payment for duties performed hearing patent appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of mistaken Patent Office fees (Act 1842)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasurer of the United States is authorized to pay back, out of the patent fund, any sum or sums of money, to any person who shall have paid the same into the Treasury... as for fees accruing at the Patent Office through mistake, certificate thereof being made to the said Treasurer by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds allowed where Commissioner certifies mistake; applies only to fees not provided to be refunded by existing laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent eligibility and general terms (Act 1842 / 1852 provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen or alien having resided one year in the United States and taken the oath of intention to become a citizen, who by his own industry, genius, efforts, and expense may have invented or produced any new and original design for a manufacture... or any new and original shape or configuration of any article of manufacture not known or used by others before his invention, and prior to application, may apply in writing to the Commissioner of Patents; the commissioner, on due proceedings had, may grant a patent therefor as in applications for patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs covered include printing of fabrics, busts/statues/bas-relief, ornaments/impressions/prints/pictures fixed on manufactured articles, new shapes/configurations. Earlier act provided that the fee in such cases should be one half the sum required by existing laws and that duration should be seven years; later statutes (1852) expanded options on term and fees (see separate entries). All regulations and provisions applicable to patents apply unless inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath acceptance abroad for applicants (Act 1842)
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath required for applicants for patents may be taken, when the applicant is not, for the time being, residing in the United States, before any minister, plenipotentiary, charge d'affaires, consul, or commercial agent holding commission under the government of the United States, or before any notary public of the foreign country in which such applicant may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits overseas oath-taking before U.S. diplomatic/consular officers or local notaries for applicants not residing in the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking and counterfeiting patent indications prohibited (Act 1842 Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person shall paint, print, mould, cast, carve, engrave, or stamp upon any thing made, used, or sold by him the name or any imitation of the name of any other person who hath obtained letters-patent for the sole making and vending of such thing, without consent... or shall affix the words 'patent,' 'letters-patent,' 'patentee,' or any word of like import, on any unpatented article for the purpose of deceiving the public, he shall be liable to a penalty of not less than one hundred dollars, with costs, to be recovered by action in U.S. Circuit or District Courts; one half paid to the patent fund and the other half to the person who shall sue for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal/penal deterrent against false marking or imitation of patentee's mark; recovery procedure and split of penalty are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to stamp or engrave date of patent on vended articles (Act 1842 Section 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: All patentees and assignees of patents hereafter granted are required to stamp, engrave, or cause to be stamped or engraved, on each article vended, or offered for sale, the date of the patent; and if any patentee or assignee shall neglect to do so, he shall be liable to the same penalty specified in the foregoing fifth section of this act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive duty on patentees/assignees to mark articles with patent date; failure subject to same penalties as false marking (see previous entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authority over patent extensions and referral to principal examiner (Act 1848)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is made to him for the extension of a patent and sixty days' notice is given, the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner having charge of the class of inventions to which said case belongs, who shall make a full report, particularly whether the invention or improvement secured in the patent was new and patentable when patented; thereupon the commissioner shall grant or refuse the extension upon the same principles and rules that have governed the board; no patent shall be extended for a longer term than seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes extension power in Commissioner; requires report by principal examiner focused on novelty/patentability at time of original patent; imposes a seven-year maximum extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording fees for assignments (Act 1848 Section 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee of one dollar for recording any assignment, grant, or conveyance of the whole or any part of the interest in letters-patent, or power of attorney, or license when such instrument shall not exceed three hundred words; two dollars when it shall exceed three hundred and not exceed one thousand words; three dollars when it shall exceed one thousand words; which fees shall in all cases be paid in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific graduated fee schedule for recording instruments based on word count; prepayment required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of clerks and salaries (Act 1848 Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be appointed two clerks to be employed in copying and recording, and in other services in the Patent Office, who shall each be paid a salary of one thousand two hundred dollars per annum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative staffing and salary provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free mailing of Patent Office annual reports (Act 1848 Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents is hereby authorized to send by mail, free of postage, the annual reports of the Patent Office, in the same manner in which he is empowered to send letters and packages relating to the business of the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives Commissioner mailing privileges for dissemination of official reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of the Interior's supervisory role over the Commissioner (Act 1849)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Interior shall exercise and perform all of the acts of supervision and appeal in regard to the office of Commissioner of Patents, now exercised by the Secretary of State; and the Secretary of the Interior shall sign all requisitions for the advance or payment of money out of the Treasury on estimates or accounts, subject to same adjustment or control as other similar estimates and accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers supervisory functions from Secretary of State to Secretary of the Interior with fiscal controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to assistant judges from Commissioner decisions; payment to judges (Act 1852)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals provided for to the Chief Judge may also be made to either of the assistant judges of the Circuit Court of the District of Columbia; and the Commissioner of Patents shall pay to such chief judge or assistant judge the sum of twenty-five dollars required to be paid by the appellant into the Patent Office on said appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands available judges for appeals and provides for payment of the judicial fee by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office annual report volume and pagination limit (Act 1859)
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual report of the Commissioner of Patents on mechanics shall be prepared and submitted so that the plates and drawings necessary to illustrate each subject shall be inserted so as to comprise the entire report in one volume not to exceed eight hundred pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting and size constraint for the Patent Office annual mechanical reports (limit on pages and inclusion of illustration plates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of appeal to the Supreme Court in patent cases regardless of amount (Act 1861)
rubrics_metrics.description: From all judgments and decrees of any Circuit Court rendered in any action, suit, controversy, or case arising under any law of the United States granting or confirming to inventors the exclusive right to their inventions, a writ of error or appeal shall lie to the Supreme Court of the United States in the same manner and under the same circumstances as in other judgments, without regard to the sum or value in controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits Supreme Court review of patent-related Circuit Court judgments irrespective of monetary threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for affidavits, depositions, subpoenas, witness attendance, privilege, and contempt in Patent Office contested cases (Act 1861 ch.88 §1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may establish rules for taking affidavits and depositions required in cases pending in the Patent Office; such affidavits and depositions may be taken before any justice of the peace or other officer authorized by law to take depositions; in any contested case pending in the Patent Office it shall be lawful for the clerk of any court of the United States for any district or territory, upon application of any party, to issue subpoenas for witnesses residing or being within the said district or territory commanding witnesses to appear and testify before any justice of the peace or other authorized officer at any time and place stated; if a witness after service refuses to appear or testify (not being privileged), the judge may enforce obedience or punish disobedience like to process of a U.S. court; witnesses shall be allowed same compensation as U.S. court witnesses; no witness required to attend more than forty miles from place of service to give a deposition; no witness shall be deemed guilty of contempt for refusing to disclose any secret invention made or owned by him; no contempt unless fees for going, returning, and one day's attendance are paid or tendered at time of service of subpoena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive procedural framework for evidence-gathering and witness compulsion in Patent Office contested cases: who may take affidavits, issuance and enforcement of subpoenas, witness compensation and travel limits, privilege for secret inventions, and contempt conditions tied to payment/tender of fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and duties of examiners in chief; appeals to Commissioner (Act 1861 ch.88 §2)
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be appointed three examiners in chief, persons of competent legal knowledge and scientific ability, whose duty, on written petition of the applicant, is to revise and determine upon the validity of decisions made by examiners when adverse to the grant of letters-patent; to revise decisions in interference cases; and, when required by the commissioner, in applications for extension; from their decisions appeals may be taken to the Commissioner of Patents in person upon payment of the prescribed fee; the examiners in chief shall be governed by rules prescribed by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a structured internal appellate layer (examiners in chief) with defined duties and an appeal path to the Commissioner, under Commissioner's procedural governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on appeals to examiners in chief and oath renewal before second examination (Act 1861 ch.88 §3)
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeal shall be allowed to the examiners in chief from the decisions of the primary examiners, except in interference cases, until after the application shall have been twice rejected; and the second examination by the primary examiner shall not be had until the applicant, in view of the references given on the first rejection, shall have renewed the oath of invention as provided in the earlier act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires two rejections before appealing to examiners in chief (except interference cases) and conditions the second examination on renewal of the oath in response to first-rejection references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner authority to restore/dispose of models and dispense with design models (Act 1861 ch.88 §5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents is authorized to restore to the respective applicants, or otherwise dispose of, such of the models belonging to rejected applications as he shall not think necessary to be preserved; same authority given in relation to models accompanying applications for designs; commissioner may dispense in future with models of designs when the design can be sufficiently represented by a drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Commissioner discretionary authority to manage physical models and to allow drawings in place of models for designs when adequate representation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner may require printing of illegible papers and may refuse recognition of patent agents for gross misconduct (Act 1861 ch.88 §8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The commissioner may require all papers filed in the Patent Office, if not correctly, legibly, and clearly written, to be printed at the cost of the parties filing such papers; and for gross misconduct he may refuse to recognize any person as a patent agent, either generally or in any particular case; but reasons for such refusal shall be recorded and be subject to the approval of the President of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality control on filing legibility enforceable by requiring printed submissions at applicant cost; sanction and de-recognition mechanism for patent agents with recorded reasons subject to presidential approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-refundability of fees; treatment of caveat fee; computation of caveator notice; prohibition of attaching additional improvements to existing patents (Act 1861 ch.88 §9 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: No money paid as a fee on any application for a patent after the passage of this act shall be withdrawn or refunded, nor shall the fee paid on filing a caveat be considered as part of the sum required to be paid on filing a subsequent application for a patent for the same invention. The three months' notice given to any caveator shall be computed from the day on which such notice is deposited in the post-office at Washington, with the regular time for transmission of the same added. So much of the thirteenth section of the earlier act as authorizes annexing to letters-patent the description and specification of additional improvements is repealed, and in all cases where additional improvements would now be admissible, independent patents must be applied for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes fee finality (no refunds), clarifies that caveat fees do not credit future applications, sets postal deposit plus transmission time as the starting point for caveator notice computation, and requires separate patents for additional improvements (no annexing to existing patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive Patent Office fee schedule (Act 1861 ch.88 §10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Established rates: On filing each caveat, ten dollars; on filing each original application for a patent except for a design, fifteen dollars; on issuing each original patent, twenty dollars; on every appeal from the examiner in chief to the commissioner, twenty dollars; on every application for the reissue of a patent, thirty dollars; on every application for the extension of a patent, fifty dollars and fifty dollars in addition on granting every extension; on filing each disclaimer, ten dollars; for certified copies of patents and other papers, ten cents per hundred words; for recording assignments/agreements/powers of attorney and other papers of three hundred words or under, one dollar; over three hundred and under one thousand words, two dollars; if over one thousand words, three dollars; for copies of drawings, the reasonable cost of making the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit, itemized fee schedule covering caveats, applications, issues, appeals, reissues, extensions, disclaimers, certified copies, recording fees by word count, and drawing copies; fees are categorical and prescriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent term options and fees (Act 1852 §11 expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for designs may be granted for the term of three and one half years, or for seven years, or for fourteen years, as the applicant may elect in his application: Provided, That the fee to be paid in such application shall be for the term of three years and six months, ten dollars; for seven years, fifteen dollars; and for fourteen years, thirty dollars: And provided, That the patentees of designs under this act shall be entitled to the extension of their respective patents for the term of seven years from the day on which said patent shall expire, upon the same terms and restrictions as are provided for extension of letters-patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives applicants elective term options for design patents with graduated fees and an explicit path to a seven-year extension under the same conditions as other patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completion and abandonment timeline; extension and hearing notice timing (Act 1852 §12)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications for patents shall be completed and prepared for examination within two years after the filing of the petition, and in default thereof they shall be regarded as abandoned by the parties thereto; unless it be shown to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Patents that such delay was unavoidable; all applications for the extension of patents shall be filed at least ninety days before the expiration thereof; and notice of the day set for the hearing of the case shall be published for at least sixty days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a two-year prosecution-completion requirement (subject to Commissioner-accepted unavoidable delay), a 90-day advance filing requirement for extension applications, and a 60-day publication requirement for hearing notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking requirement and consequences for failure to mark (Act 1852 §13)
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of any person making or vending an article under the protection of letters-patent to give sufficient notice to the public that said article is so patented, either by fixing thereon the word 'patented,' together with the day and year the patent was granted; or when impracticable, by enveloping articles and affixing a label to the package on which the notice, with the date, is printed; on failure of which, in any suit for infringement by the party failing so to mark the article the right to recover damages shall not be recovered by the plaintiff, except on proof that the defendant was duly notified of the infringement and continued after such notice to make or vend the article patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies acceptable forms of patent marking (direct on article with date or label on package) and conditions under which failure to mark bars recovery of damages unless actual notice to defendant is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing requirements for copies of patents and drawings; cost limits and parchment copy (Act 1861 ch.88 §14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to print ten copies of the description and claims of all patents which may hereafter be granted, and ten copies of the drawings when drawings accompany the patents: Provided, the cost of printing the text shall not exceed, exclusive of stationery, two cents per hundred words for each copy, and the cost of the drawing shall not exceed fifty cents per copy; one copy of the above number shall be printed on parchment to be affixed to the letters-patent; the work shall be under the direction and subject to the approval of the Commissioner, and the expense of said copies shall be paid out of the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates official printed distribution/archival copies with per-copy cost ceilings, and requires one parchment copy to be affixed to the issued letters-patent; expenses borne by patent fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed copies of letters-patent as legal evidence (Act 1861 ch.88 §15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed copies of the letters-patent of the United States, with the seal of the Patent Office affixed and certified and signed by the Commissioner of Patents, shall be legal evidence of the contents of said letters-patent in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that certified printed copies, when properly sealed and signed, are admissible and conclusive as evidence of patent contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term fixed at seventeen years from date of issue; prohibition of extensions (Act 1861 ch.88 §16)
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents hereafter granted shall remain in force for the term of seventeen years from the date of issue; and all extension of such patents is hereby prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a uniform 17-year patent term and disallows extensions for patents granted under this provision (note: later statutes amend design/other extension rules in specific contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: General repeal of inconsistent prior acts (Act 1861 ch.88 §17)
rubrics_metrics.description: All acts and parts of acts heretofore passed which are inconsistent with the provisions of this act are repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory housekeeping clause indicating that prior conflicting provisions are superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriation and repeal of printing requirement section (Act 1862)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriation for Patent Office fund and the fourteenth section of the act of March second, 1861 (authorizing printing of ten copies) is repealed (as stated in 1862 act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates appropriations and that certain printing obligations were later repealed by subsequent statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of oath-renewal requirement and salary restoration authority (Act 1863)
rubrics_metrics.description: So much of section seven of the act of July fourth, eighteen hundred and thirty-six as requires a renewal of the oath is repealed. Commissioner authorized to pay additional sums to examiners and clerks when revenue justifies so as to restore their compensation to what it was prior to reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes prior statutory requirement for renewing oath; authorizes Commissioner to restore reduced salaries when revenue permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent dating, final fee payment timeline, and consequence of nonpayment (Act 1863 §3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent shall be dated as of a day not later than six months after the time at which it was passed and allowed, and notice thereof sent to the applicant or his agent. If the final fee for such patent be not paid within said six months, the patent shall be withheld, and the invention therein described shall become public property as against the applicant: Provided, that for patents allowed previous to passage the six months shall be reckoned from date of such passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a maximum six-month window from allowance to patent-dating and final fee payment; failure to pay the final fee within six months results in withholding of patent and the invention becoming public property vis-à-vis the applicant (i.e., forfeiture to the public).
